html:
SMTO-API-0015 — This text can't be sent as a task

GUID: 219a1245-4473-4c72-a58a-640a51132397
Slug: application-command-endpoint-required
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • Text that starts with / is an SMTO command, not a task, and an empty message has nothing to do. SMTO didn't start or queue anything from it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. To run a command, type / in the message box, pick it from the Application commands list that appears, and press Enter. Commands run straight from that list; they can't be sent or queued as tasks.
  2. If you typed only /, add the command's name after it, or choose one from the list. A / on its own doesn't name a command.
  3. To ask SMTO to do something, type your request as normal text that doesn't start with /, and make sure the message isn't empty. Only plain-text requests can be sent or queued as tasks.
  4. If the text is in your queued tasks, select Edit queued prompt to fix it or Delete queued task to remove it. A queued item that is empty or starts with / will be refused each time its turn comes.

What success looks like

  • Your command runs from the Application commands list, or your request appears as a new task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying what you typed. Don't keep sending the same text unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task admission rejected the submitted text because it was empty or began with '/', or the command parser received '/' without a valid command name; application commands must use the command endpoint.

What this means

  • Prompt admission detects an application slash command or an empty queued prompt, or command parsing receives no valid command invocation. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • Prompt admission detects an application slash command or an empty queued prompt, or command parsing receives no valid command invocation.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish empty input, slash-command routing and malformed command invocation.

How to fix it

  • Send application slash commands to /api/agent/commands/execute (the composer's Application commands list does this) and send only nonblank, non-slash prompts to the task and queue endpoints. For parser errors ('Enter a command after /.', 'Expected a slash command.'), supply a command name with balanced quoting.
  • Supply a nonempty task prompt or use the application command interface for a valid slash command.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A nonempty task uses the task interface, or a valid application command uses its supported command flow.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
